lessonTitle: Consensus, Elicit and Scite for evidence

slides.title: Purpose-Built Tools for Scientific Evidence
bullets: Distinct from the general purpose assistants covered earlier in this module
Designed specifically for finding, extracting, and evaluating evidence
Can dramatically speed up work that once took hours of manual search
Still bound by the evidence hierarchy discipline from Module 6

slides.title: Fast Answers to Yes-or-No Evidence Questions
bullets: Answers direction-of-effect questions like does X reduce the risk of Y
Synthesizes whether literature supports, contradicts, or is split
Delivers an evidence-based answer in seconds
Best for a first orientation before reading individual studies

slides.title: Systematic-Review-Style Data Extraction
bullets: Summarizes articles and extracts data into comparable tables
Especially accurate on well-structured empirical studies
Speeds up comparing design, population, and results across trials

slides.title: Seeing How a Study Is Cited, Not Just That It Is
bullets: Smart Citations show whether later studies support, contradict, or mention neutrally
A heavily cited study can still be substantially contradicted
Critical signal before presenting a study as solid evidence to an HCP

slides.title: Acceleration, Not a Substitute for Judgment
bullets: All three speed up search and organization of evidence
None replaces critical judgment on methodological quality
Reading the most relevant studies directly is still necessary
Module 6 criteria on bias and limitations still apply

takeaway.title: Consensus, Elicit, and Scite each accelerate one part of evidence work, not the judgment behind it
bullets: Consensus for quick direction-of-effect answers, Elicit for structured extraction, Scite for citation context
All three save time on search, none replaces reading the key studies
Evidence hierarchy and bias criteria from Module 6 still govern every use
